item.title: Cocktail of the Day3 October 2026
item.description: Tag der Deutschen Einheit, or German Unity Day, today commemorates the reunification of Germany and is marked by political speeches, a Bürgerfest (citizens' festival) and plenty of fireworks.

item.title: Cocktail of the Day4 October 2026
item.description: Our friends across the pond have given us a reason to celebrate. In America, the 4th of October is National Vodka Day, so by extension, for the rest of us, it's International Vodka Day. Why today? I have no idea, but stateside, today is also National Taco Day.

item.title: Cocktail of the Day5 October 2026
item.description: Quiet at the back! No sniggering. Today is World Teachers Day, a chance to celebrate the role this often-maligned profession plays in all our lives.

item.title: Cocktail of the Day6 October 2026
item.description: The Mad Hatter in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland wears, as we all know, a top hat.

item.title: Cocktail of the Day7 October 2026
item.description: An American National Day marked annually on October 7th, National Frappé Day is designed to celebrate the blended coffee drink of the same name that's topped with whipped cream.

item.title: Cocktail of the Day8 October 2026
item.description: Octopuses are of course known for their eight semi-autonomous arms lined with thousands of suckers. But this remarkable creature also has blue blood coursing through three beating hearts, and highly developed intelligence with 500 million neurons in their brains and arms. Octopuses have been around for 300 million years so pre-date the dinosaurs.

item.title: Cocktail of the Day9 October 2026
item.description: On this day in 1967, Bolivian paramilitaries, working with the CIA, executed Che Guevara and spawned a thousand T-shirts.

item.title: It’s October 21st 2026 and today we are drinking a Mezcal Margarita.
item.description: Perhaps this page should read 'International Mezcal Day,' because although this 'National Day' is an all-American creation, many of us around the world feel mezcal deserves a day of its own. A day when we devotees can show our appreciation for the artisanal Mexican producers who craft this delectable agave spirit and, well, for those of us who enjoy drinking mezcal.

item.title: It’s October 22nd 2026 and today we are drinking an Añejo Almond Old Fashioned.
item.description: Happy National Nut Day! Yes, that's right – October 22nd is the day we celebrate these little nuggets of goodness. With a reputation for being the healthier snack option, nuts have, in fact, been part of the human diet for at least 800,000 years, and for good reason.

item.title: iPod's birthday
item.description: It all started in 1979 with Sony's Walkman. The portable cassette player then went digital with the invention of the first portable MP3 player in 1997. However, it was Apple's iPod, unveiled by Steve Jobs this day in 2001 that was truly game-changing, not just for how and where we enjoy music, but also for the music industry. Fortune called it Apple's 21st-Century Walkman.

item.title: United Nations Day
item.description: On this day in 1945, as the world struggled to cope with the aftermath of World War II and the new world order that had emerged, the United Nations was established with the goal of preventing such a dreadful conflict from ever happening again. The world's largest international organization, 193 nations now belong to the United Nations.

item.title: National Cat Day
item.description: The purr-fect day for all the feline fans out there, National Cat Day originated in 2005, when US lifestyle writer Colleen Paige took it upon herself to raise awareness about the number of cats that need to be rescued each year.

item.title: National Candy Corn Day
item.description: Candy corn, the sweet treat favoured by Americans in the autumn, has its own national day! Typically eaten around Halloween, candy corn was created in the 1800s by a gentleman named George Renninger, who worked at the Wunderlee Candy Company. He set out to create a bright sweet that reflected the red, yellow and orange colours of autumn and celebrated the humble corn on the cob.

item.title: The Day Of The Dead
item.description: Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos) festivities are held on November 1st (All Saints' Day) and November 2nd (All Souls' Day), a celebration which (almost) seamlessly blends Christian beliefs with activities so firmly pre-Christian that the Aztecs would probably recognise them. Traditionally, today honours deceased children and tomorrow honours adults who have passed away.

item.title: Museum of Modern Art's birthday
item.description: New York City's The Museum of Modern Art opened to the public on this day in 1929. Affectionately known as MoMA, with 300,000 books and exhibition catalogues, 1,000 periodical titles, and tens of thousands of works of architecture, design, drawing, painting, sculpture, photography, prints, films, and electronic media, it's among the world's largest and most influential contemporary art museums.
